title: Ezekiel Chapter 47 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 47 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 47 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 47.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 47, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Waters issued out from under the threshold of the house
The man measured a thousand cubits
He returned to the brink of the river
There were trees at the bank of the river
questions.correctAnswer: Waters issued out from under the threshold of the house
questions.explanation: This event is described first in the chapter, specifically in Ezekiel 47:1.

questions.question: What direction did the waters issue out from under the threshold of the house?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the waters issued out eastward, as mentioned in Ezekiel 47:1.

questions.question: What was the depth of the waters when the man measured a thousand cubits first?
questions.explanation: The waters were described as being to the ankles when measured first in Ezekiel 47:3.

questions.question: What happened when the man measured a second thousand cubits?
options: The waters were to the waist
The waters were to the loins
The waters were to the ankles
The waters were to the knees
questions.correctAnswer: The waters were to the knees
questions.explanation: The text states that the waters were to the knees after the second measurement in Ezekiel 47:4.

questions.question: What was the condition of the waters after measuring a total of three thousand cubits?
options: A river that could not be passed over
questions.correctAnswer: A river that could not be passed over
questions.explanation: This is stated in Ezekiel 47:5, describing the waters as a river that could not be passed over.

questions.question: What did the man with the line in his hand do after measuring the waters?
options: He caused me to return to the brink of the river
questions.correctAnswer: He caused me to return to the brink of the river
questions.explanation: This action is described in Ezekiel 47:6.

questions.question: What did Ezekiel see at the bank of the river?
questions.explanation: The text in Ezekiel 47:7 mentions that there were very many trees at the bank of the river.

questions.question: To which country do the waters issue out according to the text?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:8 states that the waters issue out toward the east country.

questions.question: The waters that issue into the sea shall be what?
questions.explanation: The text in Ezekiel 47:8 indicates that the waters shall be healed when brought into the sea.

questions.question: What did the man measure after he had brought Ezekiel through the waters to the ankles?
questions.explanation: The man measured another thousand cubits as mentioned in Ezekiel 47:4.

questions.question: What was the final measurement made by the man?
questions.explanation: The final measurement made by the man was one thousand cubits, as stated in Ezekiel 47:5.

questions.question: True or False: The waters rose to the loins after the second measurement.
questions.explanation: The waters rose to the loins after the third measurement, not the second, as stated in Ezekiel 47:4.

questions.question: True or False: The waters came down from under the left side of the house.
questions.explanation: The waters came down from under the right side of the house, not the left side, as mentioned in Ezekiel 47:1.

questions.question: True or False: The waters went into the desert according to the text.
questions.explanation: The text states that the waters go down into the desert, as seen in Ezekiel 47:8.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel saw a mountain at the bank of the river.
questions.explanation: The text does not mention a mountain at the bank of the river; it mentions many trees, as stated in Ezekiel 47:7.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 47 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 47 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to everything that lives where the river comes, according to Ezekiel 47:9?
questions.explanation: According to Ezekiel 47:9, 'every thing that liveth... shall live:... for they shall be healed;' indicating that the waters have a healing effect.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 47:10 promise will happen if someone goes fishing from Engedi to Eneglaim?
options: They will catch only small fish
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:10 states, 'their fish shall be according to their kinds, as the fish of the great sea, exceeding many,' promising abundant catch.

questions.question: What will happen to the miry places and marshes according to Ezekiel 47:11?
options: They shall be given to salt
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be given to salt
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:11 indicates that 'the miry places... shall not be healed; they shall be given to salt,' showing a contrast to the healing waters.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 47:12, what will grow by the river?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:12 states that 'shall grow all trees for meat,' emphasizing the provision and sustenance of the trees.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 47:13 say about the inheritance of the land?
options: The land will be divided among the tribes
It will be given to strangers
questions.correctAnswer: The land will be divided among the tribes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:13 states, 'This shall be the border... according to the twelve tribes of Israel,' indicating a division of land.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 47:14, how will the inheritance be distributed?
options: It will be equal among all tribes
questions.correctAnswer: It will be equal among all tribes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:14 states, 'ye shall inherit it, one as well as another,' indicating that the inheritance will be equal.

questions.question: What geographical feature is mentioned as the northern border in Ezekiel 47:15?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:15 mentions 'from the great sea, the way of Hethlon,' identifying the northern border.

questions.question: What cities are mentioned in Ezekiel 47:16 as part of the border?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:16 lists 'Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim' as cities that define the border, clarifying the geographical context.

questions.question: How does the healing waters in Ezekiel 47 relate to Christian life?
questions.explanation: The healing waters symbolize the renewal and restoration that God offers, aligning with the themes of spiritual rebirth in Christianity.

questions.question: What lesson can we learn from the trees mentioned in Ezekiel 47:12?
questions.explanation: The trees are for meat and medicine, illustrating that we are to provide sustenance and healing to others, reflecting God’s generosity.

questions.question: In what way does Ezekiel 47:10 encourage community engagement?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:10 encourages fishers to work together, symbolizing the importance of community in sharing resources and opportunities.

questions.question: What do the waters that flow from the sanctuary signify in a believer's life?
questions.explanation: The waters signify life and healing, indicating the vital presence of God’s spirit in a believer’s life, as illustrated in Ezekiel 47:9.

questions.question: True or False: The miry places along the river will be healed according to Ezekiel 47:11.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:11 states that 'the miry places... shall not be healed,' indicating they will remain as they are.

questions.question: True or False: The trees by the river are intended for meat and medicine according to Ezekiel 47:12.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:12 states that 'the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine,' highlighting their purpose.

questions.question: True or False: The fishers will catch fish of only one kind according to Ezekiel 47:10.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:10 mentions that 'their fish shall be according to their kinds,' indicating diversity in the catch.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 47 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 47.

questions.question: What is the northern border of the land described in Ezekiel 47?
questions.explanation: The northern border is specifically stated as 'Hazarenan, the border of Damascus, and the north northward, and the border of Hamath' in Ezekiel 47:17.

questions.question: Which side of the land is measured from Hauran according to Ezekiel 47?
questions.explanation: The east side is clearly defined as being measured from Hauran, Damascus, and Gilead in Ezekiel 47:18.

questions.question: What is the southern border of the land mentioned in Ezekiel 47?
questions.explanation: The south side is described as extending from 'Tamar even to the waters of strife in Kadesh' in Ezekiel 47:19.

questions.question: The western border of the land extends to which sea according to Ezekiel 47?
questions.explanation: The west side is stated to be 'the great sea from the border, till a man come over against Hamath' in Ezekiel 47:20.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 47:21, what is to be done with the land?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:21 states, 'So shall ye divide this land unto you according to the tribes of Israel,' implying it will be divided by lot.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 47:22, who is mentioned to inherit the land along with the Israelites?
options: The strangers that sojourn among you
questions.correctAnswer: The strangers that sojourn among you
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:22 mentions that the strangers who sojourn among the Israelites shall have an inheritance with them.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'כְּבוֹד' (kavod) in Ezekiel 47:1 mean?
questions.explanation: The word 'כְּבוֹד' (kavod) generally translates as 'glory' in Hebrew, often referring to the presence of God.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Ezekiel 47:18 regarding the description of the borders?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:18 employs parallelism in the structure of its borders, emphasizing the geographical layout in a balanced way.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of inheritance for strangers mentioned in Ezekiel 47:22?
questions.explanation: Exodus 12:48-49 speaks about the stranger being included in the Passover, paralleling the theme of inheritance for strangers in Ezekiel 47:22.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage serves as a fulfillment of the land inheritance theme in Ezekiel 47:21?
questions.explanation: Joshua 14:1-2 details the division of the land among the tribes of Israel, fulfilling the command given in Ezekiel 47:21.

questions.question: What comes before Ezekiel 47:17 in the chapter?
options: The description of the river's flow
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:16-17 details the measurements and borders of the land, with verse 17 specifically referencing the north side.

questions.question: What comes after Ezekiel 47:22 in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:23 follows and further elaborates on the inheritance of strangers in the context of the tribes of Israel.

questions.question: The waters in Ezekiel 47 symbolize what spiritual truth?
questions.explanation: The waters are described as bringing life and healing wherever they flow, indicating a spiritual cleansing and renewal.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 47, the land will be divided among the tribes of Israel. True or False?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:21 states, 'So shall ye divide this land unto you according to the tribes of Israel,' confirming that the land will be divided among them.

questions.question: Ezekiel 47 describes a river that brings forth death and barrenness. True or False?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:9 states that 'every thing that liveth, which moveth' shall live because of the river, indicating it brings life, not death.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 47 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 47 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 47:12 teach about God's provision for sanctification?
options: God provides continual nourishment and healing through His sanctuary
Sanctification is achieved solely through human effort
The fruitfulness of the land depends on human agricultural skill
Sanctification is unrelated to God's presence among His people
questions.correctAnswer: God provides continual nourishment and healing through His sanctuary
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:12 shows that the trees by the river bear fruit monthly and their leaves are for medicine because the waters issue out of the sanctuary, demonstrating God's provision for ongoing spiritual nourishment and healing.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of salvation is taught in Ezekiel 47:9?
options: Salvation brings life to all creatures wherever the river flows
Salvation is restricted to a select few with special knowledge
Salvation is only for the Israelites and excludes others
Salvation is a future hope without present effect
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation brings life to all creatures wherever the river flows
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:9 states that everything that lives where the river goes shall live, indicating that salvation brings abundant life universally where God's life-giving presence flows.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God's covenant faithfulness is taught in Ezekiel 47:22?
options: Strangers who sojourn among Israel will receive inheritance as if born among them
Covenant blessings are limited strictly to ethnic Israelites
Foreigners cannot share in God's promises
Inheritance is only for the priestly tribe
questions.correctAnswer: Strangers who sojourn among Israel will receive inheritance as if born among them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:22 teaches that strangers who sojourn and bear children among Israel shall have inheritance with the tribes, showing God's covenant faithfulness extends inclusively to faithful residents.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 47:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:8 describes the waters flowing out to heal the sea, demonstrating God's sovereign control over creation and His power to bring restoration.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Ezekiel 47:6 through the instruction given to the son of man?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 47:6, God reveals the vision and commands the son of man to observe carefully, emphasizing God's attribute of revelation in disclosing divine mysteries.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 47 prepare the theme of living water and restoration seen in the New Testament?
options: By portraying waters flowing from the temple that bring life and healing
By emphasizing the temple's destruction without hope of restoration
By focusing on ritual purity laws exclusively
By describing a permanent exile for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: By portraying waters flowing from the temple that bring life and healing
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:1-12 depicts life-giving waters flowing east from the temple, symbolizing God's restoration, prefiguring Christ's living water imagery in John 7:38.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Ezekiel 47:21-23 establish regarding the inclusion of Gentiles in God's covenant promises?
options: It anticipates the inclusion of Gentile believers who receive inheritance among Israel's tribes
It restricts inheritance strictly to ethnic Israelites
It mandates Gentiles to separate from Israel entirely
It limits covenant blessings to the Levitical priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the inclusion of Gentile believers who receive inheritance among Israel's tribes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:22-23 commands inheritance to be given to strangers as to native-born, forecasting the New Testament doctrine of Gentiles grafted into God's people (Romans 11).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 47:4 and 47:5 teach about the progression of sanctification?
options: Sanctification is progressive, increasing from ankle to swimming-depth waters
Sanctification is only external and ceremonial
Sanctification is limited to priestly classes
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification is progressive, increasing from ankle to swimming-depth waters
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 describe the waters increasing in depth progressively, symbolizing the gradual deepening of sanctification in the believer’s life.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 47:1 and 47:2 teach about God's presence and blessing?
options: God's presence flows outward from the temple, bringing blessing and life
God's presence is confined within the temple walls only
God's blessing is unrelated to His presence
God's presence causes judgment rather than blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God's presence flows outward from the temple, bringing blessing and life
questions.explanation: Both verses describe waters issuing from the temple’s threshold and gates, symbolizing God's life-giving presence extending beyond the temple.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 47:18 and 47:19 teach about God’s sovereign distribution of land among His people?
options: God sovereignly determines geographical boundaries for Israel’s inheritance
Land inheritance is decided by Israel's military conquest alone
Land boundaries are arbitrary and have no divine significance
Inheritance is unrelated to tribal distinction
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly determines geographical boundaries for Israel’s inheritance
questions.explanation: Verses 18 and 19 specify the east and south boundaries divinely appointed for Israel’s land, emphasizing God's sovereign role in allotting inheritance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Ezekiel 47:9-10 teaches a literal ecological restoration impossible in a desert. What does Ezekiel 47:8-10 actually teach?
options: The waters symbolize spiritual restoration that brings life and healing to barren places
The passage demands scientific feasibility of desert rivers
The vision is purely mythical with no theological meaning
The river only benefits the temple precinct, not the wider land
questions.correctAnswer: The waters symbolize spiritual restoration that brings life and healing to barren places
questions.explanation: Verses 8-10 depict the water flowing to the desert and sea, bringing healing and abundant fish, symbolizing God's restorative power rather than focusing on literal ecology.

questions.question: What doctrine about holy judgment and mercy is taught in Ezekiel 47:11?
options: Certain miry and marshy places remain unhealed and are given to salt, indicating holy judgment
All creation is healed without exception
Judgment is absent in God's restorative plan
Mercy overrides all aspects of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Certain miry and marshy places remain unhealed and are given to salt, indicating holy judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:11 states that the miry places are not healed but given to salt, reflecting the coexistence of judgment with mercy in God's restoration.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 47:13 and 47:14 teach about God's faithfulness to His promises concerning Israel's inheritance?
options: God faithfully fulfills the promise of dividing the land among the tribes as He swore to the fathers
God's promises are conditional on Israel's perfect obedience
The inheritance is symbolic with no literal fulfillment
The land inheritance is rescinded due to Israel's sin
questions.correctAnswer: God faithfully fulfills the promise of dividing the land among the tribes as He swore to the fathers
questions.explanation: Verses 13 and 14 affirm God's oath to the patriarchs and His intention to allot the land to the tribes, demonstrating covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God's provision for human flourishing is taught in Ezekiel 47:7?
options: God provides abundance and life as shown by the many trees along the riverbank
Human flourishing depends only on human effort
God’s provision is limited to spiritual blessings only
The barren desert is permanent and unchangeable
questions.correctAnswer: God provides abundance and life as shown by the many trees along the riverbank
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:7 notes many trees on both sides of the river, symbolizing God’s generous provision for flourishing life.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially demonstrated in Ezekiel 47:23 regarding God's treatment of strangers among Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:23 shows God’s faithfulness to His covenant by extending inheritance rights to strangers who dwell among Israel, reflecting His inclusive covenant promises.
